policy_title: Maintain Income Tax and VAT Rates
stated: The Conservative Party commits to not raising the rate of income tax or VAT in the next Parliament, as part of its plan to cut taxes responsibly.

source.quote: As well as cutting National Insurance for 29 million people, we will also not raise the rate of income tax or VAT.

bearing_set.reason: VAT directly sets prices on goods and services; a commitment not to raise it means no added consumer price burden, which is a real verdict on household affordability of essentials.
Income tax directly determines workers' take-home pay; freezing the rate (rather than raising it) has a non-negligible real-wages effect, making this a genuine verdict on pay adequacy.

A commitment to hold income-tax and VAT rates directly concerns household take-home pay and the consumer tax burden — the core indicators of O11 — and would earn a clear verdict on whether money-in-pocket is protected.

Income tax and VAT together account for the majority of UK government revenue; locking both rates constrains the fiscal toolkit and, if spending plans are maintained or grow, mechanically shifts the balance toward borrowing or cuts elsewhere — a direct bearing on the sustainability of the debt path (O12).

membership_note: The two primary bearings are O11 (the direct tax-burden pledge) and O12 (fiscal-flexibility constraint given income tax and VAT are the UK's largest revenue sources). O2 was considered but left out: VAT maintenance is status-quo preservation on prices, not an active cost-of-living move, and most food essentials are zero-rated; the effect on the inflation basket is negligible at unchanged rates. O14 (distributional) was considered but the policy changes no rate, so the income/wealth gap is not materially moved.
